references.text: Describes the place the Lord will choose as the only place for sacrifice and worship, in contrast to the warning in verse 13 not to offer sacrifices anywhere.
The positive counterpart to verse 13, specifying that burnt offerings are to be brought only to the place the Lord chooses.
Forbids the Israelites from slaughtering sacrificial animals outside the entrance of the tabernacle, reflecting a similar principle of centralized worship.
Reiterates the principle that the Passover sacrifice cannot be offered in any city, but only at the place the Lord chooses.
Shows the consequence of ignoring this command, as Jeroboam established his own places of sacrifice in Bethel and Dan.
The high places that remained in use were a violation of the prohibition against offering sacrifices on self-chosen sites.
